My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for three generations. I have about 6 mu of flat field, good sandy loam. My back is not so strong anymore at 65, and my son works in the city, so I manage alone with my wife. I do not need to think long about what to plant — it is wheat and corn, same as every year, same as my father did. The land here is suited for it. The county buys it, and I know the work.

For wheat, I till with the rotary machine after last year's corn stalks, then sow in early October. I will buy improved seed from the township seed shop — the same variety the neighbors use, not fancy hybrid, but reliable. I lay down compound fertilizer and urea as base before sowing. In spring I add more urea when the wheat starts jointing. I irrigate four times: winterizing water in November, green-up water in March, jointing water in April, and grain-filling water in May if it is dry. I spray twice — once early for disease, once in May for aphids. That is what I have always done. Yield around 450 jin per mu is normal for me.

After the wheat comes off in June, I plant corn the same day or next — no tilling, straight into the stubble. Hybrid seed gives better ears. Summer rain usually covers most of the water need, so I only irrigate once unless it is a drought year. One pesticide spray for corn borer. I apply urea twice — at planting and knee-high stage.
